method.main: Per case: 60-second baseline; admit 31 synthetic heads; prime head zero; three groups of ten unseen heads with 60-second idle pauses; ten final-head cached replays; 60-second idle; same-store process restart; 60-second idle, cached replay, 60-second idle; then independent fresh CLI controls for heads 1, 15, 30.
method.burst: After the main probe stopped, clone the final platform-rbac store into a new private server and run fifty uninterrupted full-cache-hit requests for the final head, followed by sixty seconds idle. Added because ten cached replays ended on an increasing RSS trend.
method.samples: macOS libproc PROC_PIDTASKINFO and RUSAGE_INFO_V0 every 250 ms for the server and recursively enumerated children; no command lines collected.
method.controls: Same binary as earlier worker-isolation soak; exact packets excluding only analysis_cache and tokens. No builds or other review benchmarks ran alongside measured calls.
method.pins: Older archived Nexus #963 (xlr8 module) and platform-rbac #638; one unused Go constant varies. Synthetic pins are not real commits or independent PRs. Dependency files unchanged; stale dependency_preparation omitted, with no new verification claimed.
method.timing: HTTP includes decoding; CLI includes process startup but parses output afterwards. Source admission, cloning and idle intervals are outside review latency.

interpretation: No sustained upward trend in the idle baselines of these two fixtures; this does not prove absence of leaks.
High RSS can persist after a response; a ten-request sample can catch only the rising part of retention/reclamation.

Several idle drops coincide with the blocking-thread count falling at approximately ten seconds, consistent with Tokio 1.53.3 blocking-thread retirement; this correlation does not identify every allocation.
Restart reduces RSS, but the final Nexus physical footprint was higher after restart than before it (152.0 versus 136.7 MiB); RSS is not live heap size.
Compiler cache payloads and fact counts stayed bounded; no surviving Go children or accumulating idle threads were observed.
limitations: macOS memory accounting and allocator behavior do not establish Linux cgroup limits.
RSS/footprint sums may double-count shared pages. Sampling misses short-lived children and reparented descendants, and is not an exact high-water mark.
No heap attribution: vmmap could not inspect processes under local permissions. Allocator retention versus live application caches is not fully separated.

Only two older archives, small owned-source changes and unchanged dependencies. No mixed repositories in one process, concurrent admission, or long uninterrupted new-head traffic beyond ten-request batches.
Host activity and OS caches were uncontrolled; this run is for memory investigation, not a fresh latency-gain claim.
validation: Native sampler checked with a live 48 MiB allocation, parent/child discovery and periodic output.
Python syntax and driver help checks passed.
Actual server reviews, selected fresh CLI controls, repeated packets, cache states, budgets, queue state and cleanup checked.

decision.runtime_fix: No confirmed leak or runtime change justified by this probe.
decision.restart_policy: No automatic RSS-based recycling policy introduced.
decision.next: Validate process-tree/cgroup memory and longer varied workloads in the Sentinel Linux shadow probe.
